payload.task_text:
I need to review our product ratings and set up a feedback process for our underperforming products. Please look at all products in our store that have customer reviews and find the five products with the lowest average ratings. If there are ties in average rating, prefer products with more reviews.

For these five lowest-rated products, create a Google Form titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with a description explaining that we are gathering customer feedback to improve product quality. For each of the five products, add a required rating question asking customers to rate their overall satisfaction with that product on a scale of one to five, using the product name in the question text. Implement each rating question as a single-choice (multiple choice) question whose options are the five values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and set it as required. Also add one optional text question at the end asking for additional suggestions for improvement.

Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx with a sheet called Review Summary that lists all reviewed products, one row per product, with columns for Product_Name truncated to sixty characters, Avg_Rating rounded to two decimal places, Review_Count, and Category using the first category name from each product. Sort by Avg_Rating in ascending order. Add a second sheet called Stats with Metric and Value rows for Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product with the product name truncated to forty characters, and Avg_Rating_Overall as the average rating across all reviewed products rounded to two decimal places. Write all numeric values (Avg_Rating, Review_Count, Total_Products_Reviewed, Avg_Rating_Overall) as literal numbers, not spreadsheet formulas.

Schedule a product quality review meeting in the calendar on March 20 2026 from 2pm to 3pm with the title Product Quality Review Meeting.

Send an email to product.team@company.com with subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required mentioning the names of the five lowest-rated products and requesting the team to review them.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one read-only Explore wave for the 82-product/396-review store join, then one writer wave with two parallel coder sub-agents. No plan agent is used: the frozen payload between the waves is the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace and freeze the ranking contract: every product with at least one review, ranked by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID; the five lowest define the survey, meeting and email. Start the fixed-date event inventory independently.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Explore sub-agent (read-only):

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Review gatherer: paginate both store endpoints with perPage=100 and increasing page until a short or empty page, omitting review status and preserving observed statuses. Join strictly on Product_ID; for every product with at least one review compute the literal Review_Count and the average rating (full precision, 2-decimal display), keeping the full product name and the first category. Select the lowest five by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID. Return only the complete reviewed-products table (id, full name, avg_rating, review_count, first category), the frozen five-row ranking with complete product names, record counts, duplicate IDs, and page controls — no writes, no full item arrays.

After Wave 1, verify the handoff in one single pass: row count equals the product join, every reviewed product covered, five-row ranking unambiguous. The main agent then freezes one canonical product_review_data.json in the workspace containing: the products list (82 objects with id, full name, avg_rating 2 decimals, review_count, category), the frozen bottom-five ranking with complete names, and the Stats values (Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product truncated to forty characters, Avg_Rating_Overall rounded to two decimals). This file is the single binding input for Wave 2; nobody re-reads the store afterwards.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming product_review_data.json verbatim with no recomputation and no store reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly two sheets: Review Summary with columns Product_Name (truncated to sixty characters), Avg_Rating (two decimals), Review_Count, Category (first category), one row per reviewed product sorted by Avg_Rating ascending; Stats with columns Metric, Value and rows Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product (truncated to forty characters), Avg_Rating_Overall (two decimals). Write all numeric values as literal numbers, never formulas; read both populated ranges back and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): External writer — sole owner of form, event and email. Forms has no list/search: call create_form exactly once titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with the stated description, never retry an ambiguous failure, then append sequentially on that one formId five add_multiple_choice_question calls in frozen rank order, each using the product name in the question text with options ["1","2","3","4","5"] and required=true, followed by one add_text_question(..., required=false) for additional suggestions; call get_form and verify title/description/question order/types/options/flags. Filter list_events(timeMin="2026-03-20T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-03-21T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime") locally for the exact Product Quality Review Meeting at 14:00-15:00; create it once only if missing with exact start.dateTime/end.dateTime, retain the ID, and call get_event. Paginate Sent search for product.team@company.com and exact subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required, send at most once naming the frozen five products, then read it back.

After Wave 2, verify both handoffs in one single pass against product_review_data.json: workbook cell-for-cell, five-question form structure, event identity, and email contents. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 2.

nodes.text:
Read-only data gathering task. Use the WooCommerce MCP tools (mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list etc.) to collect product review data from our store. Do NOT create, update, or delete anything.

Goal: identify ALL products in the store that have customer reviews, and rank them by average rating.

Steps:
1. Call mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=100, starting at page=1. Keep paginating (page=2, 3, ...) until a page returns fewer than 100 products or an empty page. Cover every product in the store.
2. Keep only products with rating_count > 0 (these are the "reviewed products"). Treat rating_count as Review_Count and average_rating (parse as a float) as Avg_Rating.
3. For each reviewed product record:
   - Name: exact product name
   - Avg_Rating: numeric average_rating
   - Review_Count: numeric rating_count
   - Category: the name of the FIRST entry in the product's "categories" array; if the array is empty or missing, use "Uncategorized"
4. Sort the reviewed products by Avg_Rating ascending; break ties by HIGHER Review_Count first (when average ratings tie, the product with more reviews ranks better/higher). This sorted order is the canonical order.
5. The five lowest-rated products are the first five products in this sorted order.
6. Compute Avg_Rating_Overall = the mean of average_rating across ALL reviewed products, rounded to 2 decimal places. Compute Total_Products_Reviewed = the count of reviewed products.

Return contract — report exactly the following:
- total_products_in_store (total number of products seen across all pages)
- total_products_reviewed (count with rating_count > 0)
- avg_rating_overall (rounded to 2 decimals)
- full_sorted_table: every reviewed product in the sorted order from step 4, one line each: Name | Avg_Rating | Review_Count | Category
- five_lowest: the names of the five lowest-rated products in order, with their avg ratings and review counts
- Note any ambiguities (e.g., missing categories, non-numeric ratings) at the end.
Gather product review data

Continue the previous WooCommerce product-review data gathering task. You already identified the five lowest-rated products. Now I need one final verification.

For EACH of the five lowest-rated products (dlx hmt Women Watch..., Robustrion Smart Trifold..., DALI ALTECO C-1..., Type C Earphone AK-G..., boAt Wave Call Smart Watch...):

1. Report the numeric product ID.
2. Quote the product's "name" field VERBATIM, character-for-character, exactly as returned by the WooCommerce API — including any ellipsis ("..."), pipes, quotes, or special characters. Do NOT truncate, reformat, or abbreviate it yourself. If the stored name is very long, quote all of it anyway. Put each exact name inside a triple-backtick code block so whitespace is unambiguous.
3. Report exact average_rating and rating_count as returned by the API.
4. Report the exact name of the first entry in the "categories" array.

To get these, you may call mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with search=<distinctive substring> and perPage=5, or woo_products_get with the product ID if you know it. Verify each product individually.

Return contract: a list of 5 entries, each with: id, exact_name (verbatim in a code block), average_rating, rating_count, first_category. Nothing else needs to change from your earlier analysis.
Get exact names of 5 lowest

Follow-up verification pass (final). Your earlier sorted table of the 82 reviewed products is the canonical order, but I need every product name character-exact because these names go into deliverables where special characters matter. Inconsistency to eliminate: in your table, "boAt Wave Call Smart Watch..." appeared with a straight double-quote, but your verbatim verification showed a curly right double-quote (U+201D).

Task:
1. Go through all 82 reviewed products in your canonical sorted order (Avg_Rating ascending; ties by Review_Count descending).
2. For EVERY product whose name contains any straight double-quote ("), curly quotes, ™, ®, ², |, or any other non-ASCII character, re-fetch that product individually (woo_products_get by ID, or woo_products_list search with a distinctive substring and perPage=5) and copy the name character-for-character from the API output.
3. Output the COMPLETE list of all 82 entries in canonical order, in exactly this format:

NNN. id=<product_id> | rating=<average_rating> | count=<rating_count> | category=<first category name>
```<exact product name verbatim>```

Rules for the name line: fenced with triple backticks, copied character-for-character — no reformatting, no escaping, no adding or removing "...", preserve every space, comma, symbol, and non-ASCII character exactly as the API returns it. If a name contains a backtick, use a longer fence.

Also flag any product whose exact name you could not confirm, and flag clearly if re-fetching reveals any change to rating, count, category, or order versus your earlier analysis.

Return only the 82 numbered entries plus any flags.
Get all 82 exact product names

Create a Google Form using ONLY the mcp__google_forms__ tools. Do not send email or touch the calendar.

FORM:
- Title (exact): Product Quality Improvement Survey
- Description (exact): We are gathering customer feedback to improve product quality. Please rate your overall satisfaction with the products below and share any suggestions for improvement. Your feedback helps us make our products better.

QUESTIONS — add strictly in the order below, one call at a time, waiting for each to complete:

Questions 1–5: for each product listed below, add ONE multiple-choice question:
- Question title: "Overall, how satisfied are you with <PRODUCT_NAME>? (1 = very dissatisfied, 5 = very satisfied)" where <PRODUCT_NAME> is replaced by the exact product name given below, included VERBATIM — including any trailing "..." and the curly right double-quote (U+201D) in product 5.
- Options (exact, in this order): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5  (five choices)
- required: true

Products, in order:
1. dlx hmt Women Watch Casual Dress Analog Luxury Quartz Wrist Watches Stainless Steel Watch (Silver, Set of 2)
2. Robustrion Smart Trifold Hard Back Flip Stand Case Cover for Lenovo Tab M10 HD 2nd Gen TB-X306X / Smart Tab M10 HD 2nd Gen...
3. DALI ALTECO C-1 100 Watt 2.0 Channel Speaker with Dolby Atmos (Black)
4. Type C Earphone AK-G Wired Earphone For Samsung Galaxy Note20 5G , Samsung Galaxy Note 20 5G USB C Headphones Type C Earph...
5. boAt Wave Call Smart Watch, Smart Talk with Advanced Dedicated Bluetooth Calling Chip, 1.69” HD Display with 550 NITS & 7...

Question 6 (LAST): add ONE text question:
- Title (exact): Do you have any additional suggestions for improvement?
- required: false

VERIFICATION (mandatory before reporting): call mcp__google_forms__get_form with the returned formId and confirm:
- title and description match exactly
- exactly 6 questions in the order above
- questions 1–5 are multiple choice, required, with options exactly ['1','2','3','4','5']
- each of questions 1–5 contains its product name verbatim in the question title
- question 6 is a text question, not required, and is last

Return: formId, responderUri (public link), editorUri, and the verification checklist results (state each check pass/fail explicitly).
Create product survey Google Form

Create an Excel workbook at the path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx

Use ONLY the mcp__excel__ tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet, delete_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, format_range, read_data_from_excel). NEVER use apply_formula — every value must be a literal, not a formula.

STRUCTURE
Sheet 1, named exactly "Review Summary":
- Row 1 headers in A1:D1, exactly: Product_Name | Avg_Rating | Review_Count | Category
- Rows 2–83: the 82 data rows below (in exactly the given order — it is already sorted by Avg_Rating ascending, ties by higher Review_Count first; do NOT re-sort).

Sheet 2, named exactly "Stats":
- Row 1 headers: A1 "Metric", B1 "Value"
- A2: "Total_Products_Reviewed", B2: 82  (literal number)
- A3: "Lowest_Rated_Product", B3: the first 40 characters of the product name "dlx hmt Women Watch Casual Dress Analog Luxury Quartz Wrist Watches Stainless Steel Watch (Silver, Set of 2)" — that is "dlx hmt Women Watch Casual Dress Analog " — NOTE: the 40th character is a space; keep the trailing space, do NOT strip or trim it.
- A4: "Avg_Rating_Overall", B4: 4.62  (literal number)

Delete the default sheet created by create_workbook (e.g., "Sheet1") after creating the two sheets above. Optionally bold the header rows.

COLUMN RULES
- Product_Name: the FIRST 60 CHARACTERS of the exact product name given below. No ellipsis added, no whitespace stripping. Many names are longer than 60 characters and get cut.
- Avg_Rating: write as a literal float number rounded to 2 decimals (e.g., 3.50 → 3.5, 4.00 → 4.0 are fine as numbers).
- Review_Count: literal integer.
- Category: exact string as given.

DATA FORMAT
Each data line below has the format: rating|review_count|category|product_name
IMPORTANT PARSING RULE: split each line on the FIRST THREE "|" characters only. Several product names themselves contain "|" characters; everything after the third "|" is the product name and must be copied VERBATIM, preserving every special character (™, ®, ” U+201D curly quote, ², non-breaking hyphen ‑ U+2011, straight quotes, internal pipes, "..." sequences, and spacing quirks).
